questions.q: In a distributed-memory system, a given core can directly access:
questions.explanation: Each core accesses only its own memory; cooperation is by message passing.

questions.q: MPI is best described as:
choices: A library used within sequential languages like C/C++/Fortran
questions.explanation: MPI is a message-passing library used inside conventional sequential languages.

questions.q: SPMD stands for:
questions.explanation: MPI runs one program as many processes that branch on their rank.

questions.q: Why can a pure MPI program never have a data race?
choices: Only one process runs at a time
questions.explanation: No shared variables means no two processes can race on the same variable.

questions.q: Why does MPI provide barriers but no locks?
choices: There are no shared variables to protect, but progress still needs syncing
questions.explanation: Locks protect shared variables; with none, MPI has no locks but still offers MPI_Barrier.

questions.q: MPI_COMM_WORLD is:
choices: The default communicator containing all started processes
questions.explanation: MPI_Init defines the default communicator MPI_COMM_WORLD with all processes.

questions.q: In a communicator, process ranks are numbered starting at:
questions.explanation: Ranks run from 0 to comm_sz - 1.

questions.q: MPI_Comm_size returns:
choices: The number of processes in the communicator
questions.explanation: Comm_size gives the process count; Comm_rank gives the caller's rank.

questions.q: In MPI_Send, what do the first three arguments specify?
choices: The message contents: buffer pointer, size, and type
questions.explanation: First three = contents; last three (dest, tag, comm) = destination.

questions.q: In MPI_Send, the last three arguments specify:
choices: The destination: dest rank, tag, communicator
questions.explanation: dest, tag, and communicator define where the message goes.

questions.q: Which is always true of MPI_Recv?
choices: It may buffer and return immediately
It always blocks until a matching message arrives
It uses wildcards only for the sender
questions.explanation: MPI_Recv always blocks until a matching message is received.

questions.q: The two possible behaviors of MPI_Send are:
choices: Buffer the message and return, or block until it can transmit
questions.explanation: Send either buffers (returns immediately) or blocks; behavior is system-dependent.

questions.q: For a send to match a receive, the buffer sizes must satisfy:
choices: recv_buf_sz is greater than or equal to send_buf_sz
questions.explanation: The receive buffer may be bigger than the message but never smaller.

questions.q: Who may use MPI_ANY_SOURCE and MPI_ANY_TAG?
questions.explanation: Wildcards are receiver-only; senders must give a real rank and nonnegative tag.

questions.q: Which function retrieves the amount of data actually received?
questions.explanation: MPI_Get_count reports how much data was received.

questions.q: MPI_Wtime() returns:
choices: The current time as a double
questions.explanation: MPI_Wtime returns a double; elapsed time = end - start.

questions.q: In most MPI implementations, which process can access stdin?
questions.explanation: Usually only process 0 has stdin; it reads then distributes the data.

questions.q: After calling MPI_Isend, when is it safe to reuse the send buffer?
choices: Only after MPI_Wait or a successful MPI_Test confirms completion
questions.explanation: The buffer must not be touched until completion (data copied out of it).

questions.q: MPI_Test sets its flag to:
choices: 1 if the operation completed, 0 if not
questions.explanation: MPI_Test checks an operation and sets flag = 1 if done, 0 otherwise.

questions.q: To abort an MPI computation you should call:
questions.explanation: MPI_Abort gracefully terminates all MPI processes; do not use exit/abort.

questions.q: MPI_Reduce places its result on:
choices: Only process with the max value
questions.explanation: Reduce puts the result on dest_process only; Allreduce gives it to all.

questions.q: Which collective delivers the reduction result to all processes?
questions.explanation: Allreduce is used when all processes need the global result.

questions.q: MPI_Bcast does what?
choices: Sends one process's data to all processes
Collects data from all to one
questions.explanation: Bcast sends the source's data to all processes in the communicator.

questions.q: MPI_Scatter divides the send buffer into:
questions.explanation: Scatter splits data into comm_sz pieces; piece i goes to rank i.

questions.q: How are collective communications matched?
choices: By communicator and the order in which they are called (no tags)
questions.explanation: Collectives use no tags; they match by communicator and call order.

questions.q: Why are C matrix columns awkward to send directly in MPI?
choices: C stores matrices row-wise, so column elements are non-contiguous
Columns are always larger than rows
questions.explanation: Row-major storage means column elements are scattered in memory.

questions.q: To send one column of an n by n matrix, MPI_Type_vector should use:
questions.explanation: A column is n blocks of 1 element with a stride of n.

questions.q: In MPI_Type_vector, stride means:
choices: Elements between the starts of consecutive blocks
questions.explanation: count = blocks, blocklen = elements per block, stride = gap between block starts.

questions.q: Before a derived datatype can be used, you must call:
questions.explanation: Activate a new type with MPI_Type_commit, and release it with MPI_Type_free.

questions.q: Why is one large message preferred over many small ones in MPI?
choices: Sending a fixed amount in multiple messages costs much more than one message
questions.explanation: Communication is far more expensive than computation, and many small messages cost more.

questions.q: GPGPU refers to:
choices: General-purpose computing on GPUs for problems like searching and sorting
questions.explanation: GPGPU applies GPU parallel power to general computational problems, not just graphics.

questions.q: CUDA was developed for:
questions.explanation: CUDA is Nvidia-specific; OpenCL is the portable alternative.

questions.q: Which API is designed to be highly portable across arbitrary GPUs, FPGAs, and DSPs?
questions.explanation: OpenCL is the portable API; the CUDA-vs-OpenCL question is about portability.

questions.q: In Nvidia terminology, the host is:
choices: The CPU and its associated memory
questions.explanation: Host = CPU + memory; device = GPU + memory; they are physically separate.

questions.q: A GPU is optimized for:
choices: Low latency of a single complex core
High throughput via thousands of simple cores
questions.explanation: The GPU trades latency for throughput using many simple cores in SIMD style.

questions.q: In Flynn's taxonomy, a GPU is classified as:
questions.explanation: The GPU is SIMD (data parallelism); a multicore CPU is MIMD.

questions.q: A conventional single-core CPU is classified as:
questions.explanation: A conventional CPU is SISD; a multicore CPU is MIMD.

questions.q: The GPU exploits which type of parallelism?
questions.explanation: GPUs do data parallelism; multicore CPUs do task parallelism.

questions.q: A warp is a scheduling unit of up to how many threads?
questions.explanation: A warp schedules up to 32 threads together.

questions.q: The correct CUDA execution hierarchy is:
questions.explanation: Threads form blocks; blocks form the grid launched by a kernel.

questions.q: When a kernel launches, each block is assigned to:
questions.explanation: Each block runs on one SM; its threads execute on that SM.

questions.q: The built-in variable threadIdx gives:
choices: The thread's index within its block
The block's index within the grid
questions.explanation: Idx = a rank/index; threadIdx is the thread's rank in its block.

questions.q: The built-in variable blockDim gives:
choices: The block's index in the grid
The size/shape of the thread block
questions.explanation: Dim = a size; blockDim is the block's dimensions.

questions.q: The correct 1D global thread index is:
questions.explanation: Global index = thread rank plus block rank times block size.

questions.q: For dim3 blk(3,4), the block dimensions are:
questions.explanation: Unspecified y/z fields default to 1, so blk(3,4) is 3 by 4 by 1.

questions.q: With dim3 grd(2,3) and dim3 blk(4,4,4), how many total threads start?
questions.explanation: Grid = 2x3x1 = 6 blocks; block = 4^3 = 64 threads; 6 x 64 = 384.

questions.q: CUDA requires thread blocks to be:
choices: Independent, completing regardless of other blocks
questions.explanation: Blocks must be independent and all share the same dimensions.

questions.q: An NVIDIA A100 has 108 SMs with 64 FP32 cores each. Total FP32 CUDA cores:
questions.explanation: 108 x 64 = 6912 FP32 CUDA cores.

questions.q: A CUDA kernel is defined with __global__ and always returns:
questions.explanation: Kernels marked __global__ always return void.

questions.q: A kernel is launched with the syntax:
questions.explanation: The triple angle brackets specify blocks and threads per block.

questions.q: Why is cudaDeviceSynchronize() needed after a kernel launch?
choices: Because kernel execution is asynchronous and the host must wait for completion
questions.explanation: Kernels run asynchronously; without syncing, main may terminate before threads finish.

questions.q: A __device__ function:
choices: Runs on the host, callable from the host
Runs on the device, callable from device code, is inlined and can return a value
Runs on the device but is callable from the host
questions.explanation: __device__ is device/device, inlined, and may return a value.

questions.q: Which qualifier is the default when none is specified?
questions.explanation: __host__ (host/host) is the default behavior.

questions.q: Which CUDA memory is visible to the host?
questions.explanation: Global memory is visible to all threads and the host, stored row-major.

questions.q: Which CUDA memory level is read-only?
questions.explanation: Constant memory is read-only, visible to all threads in a block.

questions.q: Shared memory in CUDA is visible to:
questions.explanation: Shared memory enables intra-block cooperation among a block's threads.

questions.q: Which set corresponds to C's malloc, free, and memcpy?
questions.explanation: cudaMalloc/cudaFree/cudaMemcpy are the device-memory analogues.

questions.q: A device pointer:
choices: Can be dereferenced freely in host code
Points to GPU memory and may not be dereferenced in host code
Is the same as a host pointer
questions.explanation: Device pointers can be passed across but not dereferenced on the host.

questions.q: In a CUDA program, which compiler handles the kernel code?
choices: The CUDA compiler, producing a separate binary
questions.explanation: Host C compiler builds CPU code; the CUDA compiler builds the kernel; separate binaries result.

questions.q: Launching a kernel with <<<1, n>>> means:
choices: One block of n threads, all on a single SM
n threads spread across all SMs
questions.explanation: One block runs on a single SM with n threads.

questions.explanation: Each canonical example maps to one of the four domains.

draw: The CSS box model with content, padding, border, margin labeled
A 3-column grid using 1fr 1fr 1fr with a 10px gap
Two overlapping boxes showing the equal-z-index stacking order
A media query block labeling its media type and condition
formulas: Box model inside to out: content, padding, border, margin
position absolute anchors to the nearest positioned ancestor, else the body
Equal z-index stacking top to bottom: fixed, absolute, relative; static bottom
Flex shorthand order is grow, shrink, basis
at-media rule = media type plus a condition
grid line 1 to line 3 spans two columns
practice: Write a media query making h1 36px only on screens at least 768px wide
Build a flex container that grows and shrinks boxes equally from a 100px basis
Convert an inline-block layout to a grid with no width calculations
Give a stuck absolute child a parent it can anchor to
watch: display inline silently ignores width and height
static positioning ignores z-index entirely
fr is a fraction of available space, not pixels
grid-column 1/3 means line 1 to line 3, which is two columns, not three
flex 0 0 100px leaves empty space and cannot shrink

questions.q: In the CSS box model, what is the correct order of areas from the innermost to the outermost?
questions.explanation: The box model nests content inside padding, inside border, inside margin (mnemonic C-P-B-M).

questions.q: Which property controls the space between an element's content and the inside of its border?
questions.explanation: Padding is the space inside the border, between content and border; margin is outside the border.

questions.q: Which property sets the space between the outside of an element's border and all other content on the page?
questions.explanation: Margin sits outside the border and separates the element from surrounding content.

questions.q: Which display value takes up the full width of its container and forces the next element onto a new line?
questions.explanation: Block elements span the full container width and start on a new line.

questions.q: For which display value can width and height NOT be set?
questions.explanation: Inline elements only take the width of their content and ignore width/height.

questions.q: Which display value behaves like inline but still accepts width and height, making it useful for building layout boxes?
questions.explanation: inline-block flows inline yet honors width/height, so boxes can be sized side by side.

questions.q: What does display none do to an element?
choices: Makes it transparent but keeps its space
Hides it and removes it from the layout
Moves it to the viewport corner
questions.explanation: display: none hides the element entirely and it takes up no space.

questions.q: Which is the default value of the position property?
questions.explanation: static is the default; the element follows the normal document flow.

questions.q: An element with position relative is offset with top/left relative to what?
choices: Its own normal position in the flow
questions.explanation: relative offsets the element from where it would normally sit in the flow.

questions.q: position absolute positions an element relative to what?
choices: Its nearest positioned ancestor, else the initial containing block
questions.explanation: absolute anchors to the nearest ancestor whose position is not static; with none, it falls back to the initial containing block (usually body).

questions.q: Which position value keeps an element in the same place on screen even when the page is scrolled?
questions.explanation: fixed is positioned relative to the viewport and stays put during scrolling.

questions.q: A child has position absolute but none of its ancestors is positioned. Where does it anchor?
choices: To its immediate parent regardless of position
To the initial containing block, usually the body
It is hidden until an ancestor is positioned
questions.explanation: With no positioned ancestor, absolute falls back to the initial containing block, typically the body corner.

questions.q: To make an absolutely positioned child anchor to its parent, what is the simplest fix on the parent?
choices: Set display block on the parent
Give the parent a fixed width
Add margin auto to the parent
questions.explanation: Giving the parent a non-static position (relative) makes it the nearest positioned ancestor.

questions.q: Which statement about z-index is TRUE?
choices: z-index works on every element regardless of position
Higher z-index always sends an element to the back
questions.explanation: A statically positioned element ignores z-index entirely.

questions.q: When overlapping elements all have the same z-index, which positioning type appears on top?
questions.explanation: At equal z-index the stacking order top to bottom is fixed, then absolute, then relative, with static at the bottom.

questions.q: Two overlapping elements share an equal z-index: one is relative, one is absolute. Which shows on top?
choices: Whichever appears first in the HTML
They render at the same level
questions.explanation: With equal z-index, absolute outranks relative in the fixed then absolute then relative order.

questions.q: A static element is given z-index 999 and overlaps a relative element with z-index 1. Which is on top?
choices: The static element, because 999 is higher
The relative element, because static ignores z-index
questions.explanation: Static positioning ignores z-index, so the relative element wins despite the lower number.

questions.q: An at-media rule is composed of which two structural parts?
choices: A media type and a condition
questions.explanation: A media query pairs a media type (e.g. screen) with a condition (e.g. min-width).

questions.q: Which media type is the most commonly used and targets computer screens, tablets, and smartphones?
questions.explanation: screen targets visual display devices and is the most common media type.

questions.q: Which media type is the default that applies to all devices?
questions.explanation: all is the default media type covering every device.

questions.q: Which media type gives speech-synthesizing browsers more information about page content?
questions.explanation: The speech type provides content information to speech-synthesizing browsers.

questions.q: Which condition applies styles only when the viewport is at least a certain width?
questions.explanation: min-width applies styles when the width is greater than or equal to the given value.

questions.q: In responsive design, which approach is described as best practice for planning screen sizes?
choices: Design for the largest screen first, then shrink
Design for the smallest screen first, then scale up
questions.explanation: Mobile-first means designing for the smallest screen first, then scaling up.

questions.q: How many dimensions does CSS Grid work in?
questions.explanation: Grid is a two-dimensional system controlling both rows and columns.

questions.q: Flexbox is best described as which kind of layout model?
questions.explanation: Flexbox is one-dimensional, aligning items along a single axis.

questions.q: What does the fr unit represent in CSS Grid?
choices: A fractional share of the available space
A percentage of the viewport height
questions.explanation: fr divides available space into fractions; 2fr 1fr is a 2:1 ratio, not fixed pixels.

questions.q: A grid item is given grid-column from line 1 to line 3. How many columns does it span?
questions.explanation: Lines 1 to 3 enclose two columns; the numbers are grid lines, not column counts.

questions.q: In the flex shorthand written as three values, what is the correct order of those values?
questions.explanation: The flex shorthand is grow, then shrink, then basis (G-S-B).

questions.q: Boxes use a flex shorthand of grow 0, shrink 0, basis 100px. What happens on a very wide screen?
choices: Boxes grow to fill the extra space
Extra space stays empty because grow is 0
Boxes wrap to a new line
questions.explanation: With grow set to 0 the boxes cannot expand, so leftover space stays empty.

questions.q: Which pair correctly matches the flex alignment properties to their axes?
choices: justify-content is cross axis, align-items is main axis
justify-content is main axis, align-items is cross axis
both align on the main axis
both align on the cross axis
questions.explanation: justify-content aligns along the main axis; align-items aligns along the cross axis.

questions.q: Match each display value to its behavior.
pairs: Full width, forces a new line, sizable
Flows inline but accepts width and height
Element hidden and removed from layout
questions.explanation: The four display values differ in flow and whether they accept dimensions.

questions.q: Match each position value to what it is positioned relative to.
questions.explanation: Each position value uses a different reference point.

questions.q: Match each box-model area to its meaning.
pairs: Where the actual content is displayed
Space between content and the border
Space between the border and other content
questions.explanation: The four nested areas define spacing inside and outside the border.

questions.q: Match each media feature or type to its role.
pairs: Applies at or above a width
questions.explanation: Media queries combine types with conditions like width and orientation.

questions.q: Match each layout concept to its description.
questions.explanation: Grid and Flexbox differ in dimensions; fr and span control sizing and merging.

draw: A timeline showing a head script with defer running after the document is parsed
A table of == versus === for pairs like 0 and '0'
A var-versus-let scope diagram around an if block
A student object with properties and a getAge/setAge method
formulas: The four characteristics: object-oriented, interpreted, dynamically typed, case sensitive
External file plus defer is the recommended inclusion; defer needs a src
Falsy values: null, undefined, 0, NaN, empty string
var is function-scoped; let and const are block-scoped; no keyword means global
try holds monitored code; throw raises; catch receives the error object
practice: Write the three function forms for the same greeting function
Create the same object in literal and constructor notation and use this
Trace push, pop, slice, and indexOf on a sample array by hand
Write a try/catch that throws an Error when a grade exceeds 100
watch: Java is not JavaScript
== does implicit conversion, so use ===; but NaN is never equal to itself
defer does nothing on embedded scripts, only external ones
length is a property, not a function; no parentheses
a variable with no declaration keyword leaks to global scope
arrow functions do not have their own this

questions.q: Which best describes JavaScript's role among the three core web technologies?
choices: It stores data on the server
questions.explanation: HTML is content, CSS is presentation, and JS describes behavior and interactivity.

questions.q: Which statement about JavaScript and Java is correct?
choices: JavaScript is a subset of Java
They are two completely different languages
questions.explanation: Despite similar names, Java and JavaScript are entirely different languages.

questions.q: Being an interpreted language executed in the browser, what does JavaScript lack that compiled languages have?
choices: A main method and a developer compilation step
questions.explanation: JS runs top to bottom via JIT with no main method and no developer-run compilation.

questions.q: JavaScript is dynamically typed. What does that mean?
choices: Values have types but variables do not
questions.explanation: Like Python, JS variables carry no declared type; the values have types.

questions.q: Using the wrong uppercase or lowercase letters in a JavaScript identifier causes what?
choices: A syntax error, because JS is case sensitive
questions.explanation: JavaScript is case sensitive, so incorrect casing is a syntax error.

questions.q: Which approach to including JavaScript is the recommended one?
choices: Embedded in a script tag in the page
An external file referenced by src
Typed into the browser console each time
questions.explanation: An external file separates behavior, enables reuse, and eases modification.

questions.q: The defer attribute causes an external script to run at what point?
choices: After the document has been parsed
questions.explanation: defer is a Boolean attribute that runs the script after the document is parsed.

questions.q: On which kind of script does the defer attribute actually work?
choices: Only external scripts with a src attribute
questions.explanation: defer works only when src is specified; it does nothing on embedded scripts.

questions.q: Placing a script in the head with no defer, and having it manipulate page content, tends to cause what?
choices: A null error because content does not exist yet
questions.explanation: Running before the page loads means the elements are absent, producing a null error.

questions.q: Which ecosystem piece is the server runtime that runs JavaScript outside the browser?
questions.explanation: Node.js is the JS server runtime environment.

questions.q: What is ECMAScript?
questions.explanation: ECMAScript is the specification defining how browsers implement JS.

questions.q: Which tool is a dependency manager in the JavaScript ecosystem?
questions.explanation: NPM manages project dependencies; WebPack and Gulp are build tools.

questions.q: How are all numbers represented in JavaScript?
choices: As doubles, there is no separate integer type
As either int or float depending on value
questions.explanation: Every JS Number is a double; there is no distinct integer type.

questions.q: Which set lists JavaScript's primitive types?
choices: Number, String, Boolean, Null, Undefined, Object
questions.explanation: The primitives covered are Number, String, Boolean, Null, Undefined, and Object.

questions.q: Which group correctly lists the falsy values in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: The falsy values are null, undefined, 0, NaN, and the empty string.

questions.q: What scope does a variable declared with var have?
questions.explanation: var is function-scoped; it leaves scope only at the end of a function, not a block.

questions.q: What happens to a var declared inside an if block when you access it after the block?
choices: It is still accessible because var is function-scoped
questions.explanation: var does not go out of scope at the end of a block, so it survives past the if.

questions.q: A variable is declared inside a function without var, let, or const. What is it?
questions.explanation: Assigning without a keyword makes the variable global even inside a function.

questions.q: Why should you prefer === over == in JavaScript?
choices: == performs implicit type conversion, giving surprising results
== does not exist in modern JS
questions.explanation: == converts types before comparing; === compares value and type with no conversion.

questions.q: What does the comparison 0 == '0' evaluate to, and 0 === '0'?
questions.explanation: Loose == converts and yields true; strict === compares types and yields false.

questions.q: What is the result of comparing NaN to itself with either == or ===?
questions.explanation: NaN never equals itself; both NaN == NaN and NaN === NaN are false.

questions.q: What is the difference between null and undefined?
choices: null is an intentionally absent value; undefined means no value was assigned
undefined is assigned deliberately; null means nothing was assigned
null is a number, undefined is a string
questions.explanation: null is deliberately assigned absence; undefined is the value of an unassigned variable.

questions.q: On strings and arrays, length is what?
choices: A method you call with parentheses
questions.explanation: length is a property, so it is used without parentheses.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three ways to define a function?
questions.explanation: The three forms are declaration, expression, and arrow function.

questions.q: Which statement about arrow functions is TRUE?
choices: They are the oldest function form
They are an ES6 shorthand that has no own this
questions.explanation: Arrow functions are an ES6 shorthand and do not have their own this.

questions.q: Which keyword creates a new instance from a constructor function?
questions.explanation: The new keyword instantiates a fresh object from the constructor.

questions.q: Inside an object method, what does the this keyword refer to?
choices: The current object the method is called on
questions.explanation: this refers to the current object on which the method is invoked.

questions.q: After an array starts as milk and tea, then push apple then pop is called, what is its length?
questions.explanation: push adds apple then pop removes the last element, returning to two items.

questions.q: What does indexOf return when the searched value is not present in an array?
questions.explanation: indexOf returns -1 when the value is not found.

questions.q: In a try/catch statement, what does the catch block receive as its parameter?
choices: The error object describing what went wrong
questions.explanation: catch takes one parameter, the error object with information about the exception.

questions.q: Match each ecosystem term to what it is.
pairs: JS server runtime outside the browser
questions.explanation: Each ecosystem name plays a distinct role: runtime, spec, manager, or framework.

questions.q: Match each primitive type to its description.
questions.explanation: The primitives differ in the kind of value they hold.

questions.q: Match each declaration keyword to its scope or effect.
questions.explanation: var is function-scoped; let and const are block-scoped; omitting a keyword makes a global.

questions.q: Match each array method to what it does.
pairs: Adds an element at the end
questions.explanation: These array methods add, remove, join, or search elements.

questions.q: Match each function or object concept to its meaning.
pairs: ES6 shorthand with no own this
questions.explanation: Functions come in several forms; new and this relate to object creation and context.

draw: The DOM tree of a small page from Document to root to children
The create, link, and remove cycle for a paragraph node
A form field showing the name attribute feeding a value read via the DOM
A mapping of the six validation checks to example inputs
formulas: The DOM is an interface to access and update content, structure, and style
Each node has 0 or 1 parent and 0 to many children or siblings
Methods with a plural s return collections; singular ones return a single node
createElement makes a free-floating node; link it with appendChild to show it
Removal trick: oldNode.parentNode.removeChild(oldNode)
addEventListener takes an event name and a handler function
Frontend validation happens after submit and before the backend, so prevent submission
practice: Write two different statements that select the same input field
From a p node, reach its parent form and its previous sibling
Change an image src both as a property and via setAttribute
Wire a button so clicking it runs a function and identify the handler
watch: getElementsByTagName returns a collection even for one match, index with [0]
HTMLCollection and NodeList are not arrays, use Array.from
CSS names in JS style are camelCase, not hyphenated
a form field with no name attribute sends nothing to the backend
validating without preventing submission lets data reach the backend anyway
selections can be injected, so always whitelist accepted values

questions.q: What is the DOM?
choices: An interface to dynamically access and update a document's content, structure, and style
questions.explanation: The DOM is an interface letting scripts access and update content, structure, and style.

questions.q: When is the DOM created?
choices: When the developer writes it manually
By the browser when the page loads
Only after the first user click
When the server sends a response
questions.explanation: The browser builds the DOM as an object representation when the page loads.

questions.q: Which node is at the very top of the DOM tree?
questions.explanation: The Document node is topmost, followed by the root element node.

questions.q: How many parents can a single DOM node have?
questions.explanation: Each node has 0 or 1 parent, and 0 to many children or siblings.

questions.q: Which method returns a single node, the first element with a given id?
questions.explanation: getElementById returns a single node matching the id.

questions.q: Which method returns a NodeList of all elements matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelectorAll returns all matches as a NodeList; querySelector returns only the first.

questions.q: Even when only one paragraph exists, what does getElementsByTagName('p') return?
choices: A collection, so you index with result[0]
questions.explanation: getElementsByTagName always returns a collection, so you access the first with index 0.

questions.q: Why is querySelector considered powerful?
choices: It understands CSS selectors like class, tag, and attribute selectors
It runs before the page loads
questions.explanation: querySelector accepts full CSS selectors to find the first matching element.

questions.q: Are HTMLCollection and NodeList arrays?
choices: No, they are objects lacking normal array methods
questions.explanation: They are objects, not arrays, so array methods like map and filter fail on them.

questions.q: How do you convert an HTMLCollection into a real array?
questions.explanation: Array.from converts a collection or NodeList into a real array.

questions.q: Which property moves from a node up to its parent?
questions.explanation: parentNode reaches the node's parent when traversing.

questions.q: Which traversal property reaches the node immediately before the current one on the same level?
questions.explanation: previousSibling moves to the preceding sibling on the same level.

questions.q: A node created with createElement does not appear on the page. Why?
choices: It is free floating until linked to the DOM
questions.explanation: Created nodes are free floating; they show only after being linked to the DOM.

questions.q: Which method inserts a new node at the end of the current node's children?
questions.explanation: appendChild adds the new node at the end.

questions.q: Which method inserts a new node before a specified sibling node?
questions.explanation: insertBefore places the new node before a given child node.

questions.q: What is the common trick to remove a node when its parent is hard to identify?
questions.explanation: Select the node, use parentNode to reach the parent, then removeChild the node.

questions.q: What is the difference between innerHTML and innerText?
choices: innerHTML includes tags; innerText is text only
innerText includes tags; innerHTML is text only
questions.explanation: innerHTML returns HTML including tags; innerText returns only the text.

questions.q: Which property gets or sets the value of a form element like an input?
questions.explanation: value is used for form elements such as input and select.

questions.q: How must CSS property names be written when set through the style property in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JS, style property names become camelCase: background-color becomes backgroundColor.

questions.q: Which two statements both correctly change an image's source to logo.png?
questions.explanation: Attributes are reachable both as properties and via setAttribute.

questions.q: What is the cleaner alternative to inline style for toggling a preset CSS class?
questions.explanation: classList.add and classList.remove toggle preset CSS classes instead of inline styles.

questions.q: Browser JavaScript is mostly event-driven. What does that mean?
choices: Code runs immediately top to bottom only
Code executes after an event fires
questions.explanation: Event-driven means code runs after some event fires, not right away.

questions.q: What is the function that runs when an event fires called?
questions.explanation: The listening function that executes when the event fires is the event handler.

questions.q: What two arguments does addEventListener take?
choices: An event name and a function name
questions.explanation: addEventListener takes the event name string and the handler function.

questions.q: Which of these is a commonly used DOM event?
questions.explanation: Submit, click, keypress, and focus are common events.

questions.q: Why must every form input have a name attribute?
choices: Without it nothing is sent to the backend
questions.explanation: The name attribute is required or the field's data is not sent to the backend.

questions.q: When does frontend validation occur relative to submit and the backend?
choices: Before the user opens the form
After submit but before the data reaches the backend
questions.explanation: Frontend validation happens after submit and before the data is sent to the backend, so submission must be prevented.

questions.q: Which validation check confirms input is one of a set of accepted values, such as a gender option?
questions.explanation: Whitelist validation confirms the value is among accepted options, guarding against injected values.

questions.q: Which validation check confirms a value falls between a minimum and maximum, like age 18 to 60?
questions.explanation: Range validation ensures a value lies within specified bounds.

questions.q: Which tool offers a full MVC architecture with two-way data binding and dependency injection?
questions.explanation: Angular is a framework with MVC, two-way data binding, and dependency injection.

questions.q: Match each selector method to what it returns.
pairs: First match of a CSS selector
questions.explanation: Some selectors return a single node, others a collection or NodeList.

questions.q: Match each DOM manipulation method to its action.
pairs: Adds a node at the end
Removes a node from its parent
questions.explanation: These methods create, link, and remove nodes in the tree.

questions.q: Match each content property to its use.
questions.explanation: Each property targets a different aspect of a node's content or styling.

questions.q: Match each validation check to its meaning.
pairs: Input is not empty or null
questions.explanation: The validation checks cover presence, format, range, and whitelist among others.

questions.q: Match each library or framework to its description.
questions.explanation: Each tool is known for a distinct strength and is either a library or framework.
